transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Maestro Salieri, thank you for seeing me. Please, sit. I have reviewed your case with great care.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, Doctor, thank you for your attention to my case. I must admit, I am quite anxious to hear your findings. Please, do not keep me in suspense any longer.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Maestro, I must be candid. Your symptoms — the trembling, the headaches, the confusion — do not fit a single clear diagnosis.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, that is disconcerting to hear, Doctor. Do continue. What do you suspect might be the cause of these troubling symptoms?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: It could be nervous exhaustion from overwork, Maestro. The demands of the court, your compositions, the endless rehearsals... But it could also be the early signs of something more serious affecting the brain.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Nervous exhaustion... I suppose my passion for music and the duties at court have taken their toll on me. But the thought of a more serious ailment is disconcerting. What would you recommend as the next course of action, dottore?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I must insist you reduce your conducting duties immediately. The strain on your nerves is evident. You must submit to further examination over the coming weeks. We must observe the progression of these symptoms.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Reduce my conducting duties... It pains me to consider stepping back from my work, but I understand the necessity of prioritizing my health. I shall follow your advice, Doctor, and submit to further examinations as needed. I trust your expertise in guiding me through this challenging time.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Your cooperation is wise, Maestro. I cannot yet say whether your hands will recover their steadiness, but rest and observation are our best allies now.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Doctor, for your honesty and guidance. I shall rest as needed and trust in your expertise to guide me through this challenging time. My hands are indeed crucial to my work, but I understand that my health must come first. I appreciate your efforts to help me regain my strength and well-being.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Your understanding does you credit, Maestro. We shall meet again next week. Until then, no scores, no baton. Let the music rest within you for a time.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I shall mark the appointment in my calendar, Doctor. Your instructions are clear, and I shall refrain from scores and conducting until our next meeting. I shall let the music rest within me as you suggest. Until we meet again, I bid you farewell and thank you for your care.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Farewell, Maestro. May the quiet bring you clarity. I shall see you next Tuesday.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Farewell, Doctor. I shall await our next meeting on Tuesday. May this time of quiet indeed bring me the clarity I seek. Grazie.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Grazie a lei, Maestro. A presto.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: A presto, Doctor. Grazie ancora.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *The physician gives a respectful nod, gathering his medical bag, and quietly exits the room, leaving Salieri to his thoughts.*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *As the physician leaves, I sit in silence, my mind filled with a mixture of concern and determination. The room feels emptier without the doctor's presence, but I know that this solitude is necessary for reflection and healing. I close my eyes, letting the music within me speak in whispers, waiting for the stillness to bring the clarity I seek.*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *The door clicks shut softly. The physician's footsteps fade down the marble corridor. The silence in the room deepens, broken only by the distant sound of a carriage on the cobblestones outside.*
